paper.title: Pareto Active Learning with Gaussian Processes and Adaptive Discretization

settings.name_in_paper: Pareto active learning (epsilon-accurate Pareto set identification) with an m-output GP-sampled objective on a well-behaved compact metric space
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Multi-objective (vector-valued) rewards: Pareto set identification with m >= 2 objectives.
unmapped: vector-valued objective f: X -> R^m with m >= 2 objectives; goal is an epsilon-accurate Pareto set
design space is a well-behaved compact metric space (tree of cells with geometrically decaying radii) with metric dimension D_1
learner knows the metric-dimension and Hölder constants (D_1, C_k, alpha) used to set V_h, and the tree partition
settings.definition_quote: We consider the problem of optimizing a vector-valued objective function f sampled from a Gaussian Process (GP) whose index set is a well-behaved, compact metric space (X,d) of designs. We assume that f is not known beforehand and that evaluating f at design x results in a noisy observation of f(x).

symbols.g_eps: min{T >= 1 : sqrt(gamma_T/T) < epsilon}, where epsilon = min_j epsilon^j
symbols.gamma_T: maximum information gain of the m-output GP after T evaluations

conditions: zero-mean GP prior, Gaussian noise N(0, sigma^2)
tuning: beta_tau = 2 log(2 m pi^2 N^{h_max+1} (tau+1)^2/(3 delta))
